children: South Korean security services company S-1 is set to report higher earnings per share under its strong shareholder-return plan, Daiwa Capital analysts Thomas Y. Kwon and Joon Lee say in a note. The company aims to increase its total shareholder return ratio to 134% for 2026-2028 from 53% in 2023-2025, after announcing an additional 450 billion won in share buybacks and cancellations earlier this week, they note. The Samsung Group affiliate is also poised to benefit from a new building management system contract with a captive customer. They analysts raise their EPS estimates for S-1 by 7%-23% for 2027-2028. Daiwa upgrades the stock to buy from outperform and lifts its target price to 105,000 won from 76,000 won. Shares are last 0.7% higher at 98,300 won. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
